chunks: Al-Husayn ibn Said from Ibn Sinan, from one who informed him, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
I asked him about a man who cut off the head of a dead man. He said: Upon him is the blood money (diyah), for his sanctity when dead is like his sanctity when alive.

key_terms.الدِّيَةُ: Blood money or compensation for death/injury

ai.seo_question: What is the blood money for cutting off the head of a dead person?
ai.summary: In this ruling from Imam al-Sadiq (AS), the sanctity (hurma) of the deceased is equated to that of the living, establishing that severing the head incurs the full blood money (diyah). This principle underscores the continuity of bodily integrity and honor in Shia jurisprudence, extending legal protections beyond death to maintain the dignity of the human form.
